question: Ramesh purchased 130 books at the rate of ₹200 each and sold half of them at the rate of ₹300 each, one-fifth of them at the rate of ₹350 each and the rest at the cost price. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let's find the average profit per book directly using fraction parts:

Profit on 1/2 of books = ₹300 − ₹200 = ₹100

Profit on 1/5 of books = ₹350 − ₹200 = ₹150

Average profit = (1/2 × 100) + (1/5 × 150) + (3/10 × 0) = 50 + 30 = ₹80

Profit % = (80 ÷ 200) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of books = 130

Cost price of each book = ₹200

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6d77576598769cd2f2fb6892aff4fdff11bee05f01fa05c005413acd3bc1b95.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP of 130 books = 130 × 200 = ₹26,000

⇒ SP of half the books (130 ÷ 2 = 65) = 65 × 300 = ₹19,500

⇒ SP of one-fifth of the books (130 ÷ 5 = 26) = 26 × 350 = ₹9,100

⇒ Remaining books = 130 − (65 + 26) = 39

⇒ SP of remaining books at CP = 39 × 200 = ₹7,800

⇒ Total SP = 19,500 + 9,100 + 7,800 = ₹36,400

⇒ Profit = 36,400 − 26,000 = ₹10,400

⇒ Profit % = (10,400 ÷ 26,000) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit/Loss

When different parts of a total quantity are sold at different profit or loss percentages, the net profit/loss % is the weighted sum of individual percentages.

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP). Profit percentage is always calculated on the base of Cost Price: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
